name: oneKampus
tagline: One platform for schools and coaching institutes — institute management, an LMS with payments, proctored exams and hiring — on web and mobile with a single sign-in.
problem: Institutes juggle separate tools for admissions, fees, classes, exams and hiring, and none of them talk to each other. oneKampus puts all four in one product, with one login across a web app and a mobile app.

decisions.title: A modular monolith, not microservices
decisions.body: One deploy and in-process calls keep a solo-run product cheap and debuggable. Boundaries are enforced by Modulith tests instead of the network, so any module can be extracted later.

decisions.title: A Postgres schema per module
decisions.body: Each module owns its tables and migrations, which isolates change and makes extraction possible. The cost: no cross-schema foreign keys and four connection pools on a small server.

decisions.title: WebRTC signalling over HTTP polling
decisions.body: Polling every second through the existing API avoided running a WebSocket server behind Cloudflare and Caddy. It trades a little latency and request load for much simpler infrastructure.

resumeBullets: Built a Spring Boot 4 modular monolith (Spring Modulith) with 4 modules — institute management, LMS, proctored exams, hiring — 387 REST endpoints and 108 JPA entities, one Postgres schema per module.
Shipped a Next.js web app (65 pages) and React Native app (31 screens) on one SSO token; Stripe checkout with signed webhooks, WebRTC interviews, CI to Docker on Lightsail.

decisions.title: One deployment for every tenant
decisions.body: Routing on the Host header means one app serves every client site — a single $7/month box. The trade-off is a shared failure domain, which suits small sites.

decisions.title: Content as JSONB, sections as config
decisions.body: A new kind of website needs no migration, just a new config module. Less relational integrity, so validation happens in Zod instead of the database.

decisions.title: Code sites isolated on their own origin
decisions.body: Client-written React runs only on its own host, never next to the admin panel — so a client's JavaScript can never touch an admin session.

resumeBullets: Multi-tenant Next.js 15 platform hosting client sites by subdomain or custom domain, with Caddy on-demand TLS and 29 website blueprints; live at sites.onekampus.com.
Role-based admin and client portals, in-browser code editor with esbuild-wasm preview, GitHub-webhook deploys with rollback, WhatsApp/email enquiry alerts.

name: Music streaming app
tagline: Spotify-style streaming with live “listening now” presence and chat, an admin studio, and a native mobile player — deployed with Docker and Caddy on AWS Lightsail.
problem: A music app where friends can see what each other are playing in real time and message about it. It streams uploaded songs from S3 and a catalogue pulled from YouTube and Jamendo.
note: Started from an open-source realtime Spotify-clone tutorial. My work: the entire React Native app, moving storage from Cloudinary to S3 and auth from Clerk to JWT, three external catalogues, the catalogue cache, and the production deployment.

decisions.title: Cache the catalogue for a day
decisions.body: Each YouTube category costs ~101 of 10,000 free daily quota units. A 24-hour on-disk cache that serves stale data on provider failure keeps the app inside the free tier.

decisions.title: One player, two engines
decisions.body: A single interface switches between native TrackPlayer and a YouTube WebView, giving full-length playback without breaking YouTube's terms — at the cost of two playback paths.

decisions.title: In-memory presence on one box
decisions.body: Presence lives in a Map in one container: simple and instant. Scaling past one instance would need a Redis adapter, a known next step.

resumeBullets: Extended an open-source music app: built the full React Native player, real-time presence and chat (Socket.IO), S3 streaming via presigned URLs, and JWT auth.
Deployed API, web and admin on three subdomains (Docker, Caddy, Lightsail) with a 24-hour catalogue cache to stay inside YouTube API quotas.

tagline: A full food-delivery platform: customer web and app, a rider app, a restaurant Partner Hub and an ops console — five front ends on one Spring Boot API, with live order tracking over WebSockets.
problem: Food delivery needs four parties to move in sync: customer, restaurant, rider and operations. Dabba runs all four on one API, with every status change pushed live to every screen.

decisions.title: Modules, not microservices
decisions.body: Boundaries are enforced by Spring Modulith tests and events are stored before delivery, so a crash never loses a 'settle this order' message — without running eight services for one city.

decisions.title: Redis GEO instead of PostGIS
decisions.body: Nearest-rider search runs in under a millisecond with GEOSEARCH. Zones are centre + radius for now; PostGIS can be added later without changing the API.

decisions.title: Free sign-in, no paid SMS
decisions.body: Customers use Google or a 6-digit email code and riders use phone + password, so sign-in costs nothing per user.

resumeBullets: Built a food-delivery platform on one Spring Boot 4.1 modular monolith (8 Modulith modules, 131 REST endpoints, 31 JPA entities) serving customer web, Partner Hub, ops console and two React Native CLI apps.
Live order flow over STOMP WebSockets, Redis GEO rider dispatch, idempotent checkout with server-side re-pricing, double-entry ledger in paise; live at dabba.onekampus.com.
